title: SBI: the same posted-rate bucket moves from 6.50% to 6.25%
summary: Two SBI archive observations list 6.50% and 6.25% for the same general-public domestic INR deposit bucket: below INR 3 crore, one year to less than two years. The decrease is 0.25 percentage points.
facts: Archive observations: 31 May and 8 July 2025 | Selected-column applicability dates: 16 May and 15 June 2025 | Quoted rates: 6.50% → 6.25% per year | Matched amount bucket: Below INR 3 crore
notes: Sparse observations do not identify the earliest actual adjustment. Column applicability dates do not prove when this tenor first changed. There is no causal policy pass-through or realized customer-rate inference; callability is not explicit in the selected table.

title: PNB: one year and 390 days have different quotes
summary: The 26 May 2025 PNB archive lists 6.70% for one year, 6.80% for more than one year to 389 days, and 7.00% for 390 days in the same general-public Domestic/NRO table below INR 3 crore. Selecting the highest nearby-tenor rate would change the product being compared.
facts: One year: 6.70% per year | More than one year to 389 days: 6.80% per year | 390 days: 7.00% per year | Selected-column applicability date: 14 May 2025
notes: This is a comparison within one document, not a rate-change event. The panel uses a nominal 365-day point but retains the bank’s one-year label. A shared Domestic/NRO table does not establish terms for every non-resident product.

title: Axis: three dates in one archived rate card
summary: An Axis PDF named for 8 June 2023 was archived on 10 June. Its first-page retail table states applicability from 18 May and quotes 6.75% for general deposits below INR 2 crore, one year to one year and four days. The 8 June date on page 3 belongs to deposits of INR 5 crore and above.
facts: Selected retail table: 18 May 2023; 6.75% per year | Filename and bulk-table date: 8 June 2023 | Archive observation: 10 June 2023 | Selected tenor: One year to one year and four days
notes: Saving a dated rate card on 10 June does not establish that its retail quote was active that day. The table date is not a proven first-change date. Different amount schedules are not successive versions of the same product.
